union.text: Pate Island with Pate town, Siyu and Faza (the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

land.text: Pate Island and the Lamu coast, which came under British protection after the German protectorate of Wituland was renounced on 1 July 1890

successors.note: Which state took the land in 1895 is not on the Pate page ('a sultanate ... until 1895'); the Sultanate of Zanzibar page has the British proclaiming a protectorate on 1 July 1895 (East Africa Protectorate); the Wituland page has a British protectorate declared on 18 June 1890.

capitals.name: Pate Town
capitals.note: The page names no formal capital, only Pate Town as the centre of the sultanate 'from the 13th-19th centuries'; from 1858 the Nabhani domain is Wituland, whose capital was Witu (Wituland page).

correction.text: Pate Island with Pate town, Siyu and Faza (the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1203-1895: Pate Island with its towns. The page names Pate Town, Faza and Siyu and gives no area, boundary or mainland holding; 'in the 14th century, Pate was so powerful that it had conquered most of the towns on the Swahili coast', which is a claim of dominance, not a territory, and is not drawn. After 1858 the domain is called Wituland, on the mainland north of the Tana (about 3,000 km2, Wituland page), which this keyframe does not include.

region.text: Pate Island with Pate town, Siyu and Faza (the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

ledger.note: 1203: the Nabhani family re-found the sultanate of Pate. 'It was re-founded in 1203 by members of the Nabhani family, also from Oman'; the town 'was founded by refugees from Oman in the 8th century' and 'Archeological evidence suggests Pate was a prominent location in local trade networks by the 10th century'. The page names the town, not a boundary.

region.text: Pate Island with Pate town, Siyu and Faza (the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

ledger.note: January 1844: Said's army lands at Faza. After the Sheikh of Siyu and the new Sheikh of Pate repudiated his authority in 1843, an army of about 2,000 under Amir Hemed 'landed at Faza in January 1844', was ambushed near Siyu and withdrew after three weeks without a victory.

region.text: Pate Island with Pate town, Siyu and Faza (the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

ledger.note: 1845: Siyu defeats Said again. 'In 1845 Siyu gave Seyyid Said one of his greatest military defeats'; the Omani commander Amir Hemed was killed.

1858: the domain becomes Wituland. 'From 1858 on it was the domain known as Wituland' (Pate page); the Wituland page has Witu 'fully independent from nominal' Pate rule by then, founded in the 1810s, so the two pages draw the line between Pate and Witu differently (see notes).

region.text: Siyu, on the north coast of Pate Island (approximate position)

ledger.note: 1863: Siyu submits to Zanzibar. 'When Siyu finally succumbed to Zanzibar's dominance, under Sultan Majid in 1863', one of the last towns of the Swahili coast to do so. Whether Pate town submitted with it is not on the page.

region.text: Pate Island with Pate town, Siyu and Faza (the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

ledger.note: 1895: the end of the Pate sultanate. 'The Pate Sultanate was a sultanate from at least the beginning of the 13th century until 1895.' The page does not say who took it; the Sultanate of Zanzibar page has the British proclaiming their protectorate over the Kenyan coast on 1 July 1895.

wars.name: Battle of Shela
wars.outcome: Failure: 'The attempt failed totally, and many were killed'; Pate, allied with the Mazrui of Mombasa, had tried to subject Lamu.
wars.note: Lamu later 'subjugated' Pate, 'in the late 19th century'. No border moved in 1813.

wars.name: Omani expedition against Siyu and Pate

zones.text: Pate Island with Pate town, Siyu and Faza (the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

wars.outcome: Pate and Siyu victorious: Said's force of about 2,000 withdrew from Siyu in 1844 and was beaten again in 1845; Siyu submitted to Zanzibar only in 1863.

certainty.note: An island town and its neighbours: no page gives a boundary.

sources.title: Pate Sultanate
sources.note: Pate: 1203 Nabhani refounding, Battle of Shela 1813, Siyu and Pate against Said 1843-1845, Siyu submits to Zanzibar 1863, Wituland from 1858.

sources.title: Wituland
sources.note: Witu: established c. 1810, independent of nominal Pate rule by 1858, German protectorate 27 May 1885, British 18 June 1890; end 1905/1923.

notes:
New state (Cliopatria has no Pate row). The Pate page is thin: no rulers, no capital, no infobox, no area, no account of 1895. Dated lines used: the re-foundation in 1203, Shela 1813, the Siyu/Pate revolt against Said 1843-1845, Siyu's submission to Zanzibar in 1863, Wituland from 1858, 'until 1895'.

Not drawn, because undated or unlocated on the pages: the claim that 'in the 14th century, Pate was so powerful that it had conquered most of the towns on the Swahili coast' (a list of towns, not a territory) and the 18th-century 'Golden Age of Pate'; the Portuguese destruction of Faza in 1587.

Disagreement to settle: the Pate page makes Wituland (from 1858) the Nabhani domain of the same sultanate and ends it in 1895; the Wituland page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wituland, opened) makes Witu a state of its own, 'established c. 1810', 'fully independent' of Pate in 1858, a German protectorate from 27 May 1885, a British protectorate on 18 June 1890 with Germany renouncing on 1 July 1890, and ending in 1905 or 1923. Witu has its own dossier in this batch (wituland); its protectorate events (German 27 May 1885, British 18 June 1890) are for the dossiers of the German Empire and British Colonial Empire to record with 'wituland' as the vassal.

Coordinates for Pate Town (2.12 S, 41.07 E) and the Pate Island and Siyu zones are the researcher's reading, not on the page. Gazetteer names needed: Pate, Siyu, Faza, Witu.
